item.title: Public Star Party — Sat Sep 5, 8:00 PM — Robert Ferguson Observatory
item.description: Public Star Parties are the heart of the Robert Ferguson Observatory—your monthly invitation to experience the wonder of the night sky like never before. Whether you’re a lifelong astronomy enthusiast or simply curious about what lies beyond our planet, these gatherings offer something magical for everyone. Each month includes a variety of engaging astronomy presentations led by our expert docents. You’ll hear fascinating stories about the cosmos and the science behind some of the objects you’ll soon be observing. These talks set the stage for an unforgettable night under the stars. Step outside into the darkness of Sugarloaf Ridge State Park, where the skies open up in breathtaking clarity. You’ll have the chance to explore the universe through three of RFO’s massive telescopes, each powerful enough to reveal extraordinary detail: lunar craters, planets, star clusters, glowing nebulae, distant galaxies, and more. item.title: Culinary Garden Cooking Classes at Quivira Vineyards — Sun Sep 6, 12:00 AM — Quivira Vineyards and Winery
item.description:
Join an immersive, hands-on culinary series at Quivira Vineyards, offered June 7-November 15 from 11 AM - 2 PM. Led by Estate Chef Julia, guests begin in the organic estate garden harvesting seasonal ingredients before moving to the open-air kitchen to prepare a garden-inspired, multi-course meal. This interactive experience highlights the connection between garden, vineyard, and kitchen, while teaching practical culinary techniques. The evening concludes with a shared meal paired with Quivira wines in a beautiful estate setting. Each date features a different focus, including handmade pasta, masa and tacos, stuffed pasta, global dumplings, and seasonal pie baking. Space is limited for these unique seasonal classes.

item.title: Watercolor | Building Technique II, with Nancy Ballard — Tue Sep 8, 10:00 AM — Petaluma Arts Center
item.description:
Building on the skills and confidence you developed in the first class, this watercolor workshop invites you to take your ideas a step further. Explore how a simple sketch, thoughtful composition, and expressive use of color can transform an idea into a finished painting.
We'll work larger and bolder while exploring watercolor techniques including:
Wet-on-wet paintingLoose interpretation and expressive mark-makingCreating shadows and depthEnhancing backgroundsWorking in black and whiteExploring the many variations and possibilities of mixing greens
Bring a favorite photograph, a live flower or small plant, or even a meaningful memory to use as inspiration. No matter where you are in your artistic journey, you'll be encouraged to experiment, have fun, and focus on the larger picture rather than striving for perfection. There are no mistakes in art—only opportunities to explore.
Please Note: There will be a $10 supply fee paid directly to the Nancy on the day of the class.

item.title: Last West: An evening exploring the making of Roadsongs for Dorothea Lange — Sat Sep 12, 5:00 PM — Western Hills Garden
item.description:
As dusk falls over Western Hills Garden, join poet and playwright Tess Taylor and director Ciera Eis for an intimate evening inside the making of Last West: Roadsongs for Dorothea Lange.
Hear readings from the play, watch an unforgettable slideshow of Dorothea Lange's California photographs, and go behind the scenes of an extraordinary production in development.
Tess and Ciera will be in conversation about the images, voices, and stories at the heart of Last West — Lange's road journals, her Dust Bowl migrations, her portraits of ordinary Californians navigating water, land, work, and belonging — and what her vision asks of us now.
The evening will also open into a broader conversation about the vital role spaces like Western Hills Garden play in sustaining artists and art-making in California today. Wine, snacks, and a light soup and salad supper included.
